data.exact_reserve_text: Included within net claims incurred of GBP 473.6m (2019: GBP 302.5m) is a deterioration of GBP 7.9m (2019: deterioration of GBP 8.4m) to claims reserves established at the prior year end principally due to unfavourable developments on Property, Third party liability and Accident and Health with partially offsetting favourable developments across the other classes.

prior_year_events.impact_description: Claims in respect of the Covid-19 pandemic total GBP 128m net of reinsurance recoveries, adding 27% to the net loss ratio. The discontinued Contingency class, written on the 2018 and 2019 years of account, was the most severely impacted line as a result of the large number of event cancellations following the restrictions imposed in an effort to contain the virus. Other classes were also impacted, to a lesser extent, as a result of business interruption (UK Property and Treaty Property classes), the recessionary impacts of the pandemic following the sharp decline in economic activity (Casualty, Political Risk and Treaty classes) as well as from an increase in medical expenses and travel related claims (Accident and Health).

data.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 1861 experienced a prior year reserve strengthening of GBP 7.9 million in 2020, representing a 1.73% increase relative to its opening gross claims outstanding. This deterioration was primarily driven by unfavourable developments in Property, Third party liability (Casualty), and Accident and Health classes. Additionally, the report highlights a significant impact from the COVID-19 pandemic, which resulted in GBP 128 million (net of reinsurance) in claims for the 2018 and 2019 years of account, particularly affecting the discontinued Contingency class, as well as Property, Treaty, Casualty, Political Risk, and Accident & Health lines due to event cancellations, business interruption, and recessionary effects.
